t: Chang'e-6 Samples Reveal Impact History of Moon's South Pole-Aitken Basin
r: Returned samples from China's lunar missions are finally shedding light on the violent impacts that shaped the Moon's largest and deepest basin. Combining orbital data with ground samples gives researchers a clearer picture of lunar evolution.
s: Analysis of lunar samples returned by the Chinese Chang'e-6 mission, combined with in-situ data from Chang'e-4, details the impact chain reaction that formed the massive South Pole-Aitken basin on the Moon.

t: The Milky Way Shines Over Lençóis Maranhenses National Park
r: This stunning astrophotography captures the Milky Way arching over the white sand dunes and dark lagoons of Brazil's Lençóis Maranhenses National Park. It's a gorgeous reminder of how terrestrial landscapes enhance our view of the cosmos.
s: Astronomy Picture of the Day features a vibrant shot of the Milky Way shining brightly in the sky above the white sand dunes and dark lagoons of Lençóis Maranhenses National Park in Brazil.

t: Gray Wolves May Help Wild Blueberries Spread in Northern Minnesota
r: Researchers in northern Minnesota have discovered that roaming gray wolves play an unexpected role in seed dispersal for wild blueberries. It's a fascinating look at regional ecology and unexpected wildlife connections.
s: Researchers in northern Minnesota found that gray wolves roaming the northern woods may help spread wild blueberries, with studies showing high seed recovery rates in scats.

t: Hera Mission Unveils Close-Up Images of Asteroid Moon Dimorphos
r: The European Space Agency's Hera mission has returned new, detailed images of the Didymos system and its battered moon Dimorphos following past impact tests. These observations help planetary defense researchers understand asteroid structural integrity.
s: The Hera mission has revealed new images of the asteroid Didymos and its moon Dimorphos, offering a closer look at the celestial body following previous impact experiments.

t: Microsoft Studies How Inconsistent Documentation Affects AI Coding Agents
r: Software documentation inevitably drifts from actual product behavior, but understanding how this impacts AI coding assistants is crucial for modern engineering. This Microsoft research offers valuable insight into agent reliability and API friction.
s: A Microsoft engineering blog post explores how documentation drift affects AI coding agents, examining the friction caused when reference pages and how-to guides disagree.

t: Celebrating Poul Anderson at 100
r: Poul Anderson's enduring science fiction remains a touchstone for speculative fiction fans a century after his birth. Looking back at his prolific career highlights why reliable, imaginative world-building stands the test of time.
s: To mark the late author's 100th birthday, a retrospective looks back at five of Poul Anderson's most memorable short works and enduring contributions to speculative fiction.

t: Euclid's Record-Setting Quasar Probes Black Hole Formation
r: The ESA's Euclid Space Telescope has identified a record-setting quasar at redshift z=8.13, pushing our view back to about 630 million years after the Big Bang. Finding supermassive black holes this early in cosmic history is a major puzzle for astronomers, and each distant detection helps test theories of how they formed so quickly.
s: Euclid's discovery breaks previous distance records by roughly 40 million years, giving scientists an unprecedented glimpse into the early universe. Capturing light from just 630 million years post-Big Bang helps researchers piece together how massive black holes grew so rapidly in the cosmic dawn.

t: A New Discovery is Re-Drawing the Map of the Milky Way
r: New research reveals that star formation is actively occurring right in the Milky Way's central bar, overturning previous assumptions and observations of other barred spiral galaxies. A PhD student's work demonstrates that a massive rotating structure near the galactic center drives shock fronts through gas clouds, sparking new stellar nurseries.
s: Fresh observations show star formation happening within the Milky Way's central bar, contrary to past models. A massive rotating structure is compressing gas clouds with intense shock fronts, creating prime conditions for new stars to ignite near the core of our galaxy.

t: Daisy Chaining Stepper Motors
r: Controlling dozens of stepper motors usually requires a rat's nest of wiring or complex multi-channel controller boards. This clever open project puts a smart ESP32-S3 and driver chip directly on each NEMA 17 motor, letting builders daisy-chain commands much like addressable LED strings.
s: Josh Rogan's CANBUS Stepper project simplifies multi-motor setups by packing a microcontroller and driver onto a compact board mounted straight to each NEMA 17 motor. Commands are passed down the line from a single connected node, eliminating massive wiring harnesses for complex builds.

t: Game Boy Museum on a Cart Gives the Gift of Knowledge
r: Distilling an entire online history museum onto a monochromatic 160x144 Game Boy screen is an incredible exercise in retro constraints and data packing. It highlights the ingenuity required to make readable text and images fit within tiny hardware footprints.
s: Developer Marcel managed to pack his entire Game Boy memorabilia museum onto a single standard game cartridge. Overcoming tight resolution limits and font spacing issues, the project preserves hardware variants and obscure peripherals right on vintage handheld hardware.

t: Touching a Spinner Makes Things Feel Sticky or Slippery, in VR
r: Haptic feedback in virtual reality often relies on simple vibration rumble packs, but simulating actual surface texture requires clever perceptual tricks. By dynamically manipulating the relative speed of a touched wheel, researchers have figured out how to make virtual honey feel sticky and virtual oil feel slick.
s: The Surf-Roll virtual reality haptic project uses a spinning wheel under the user's fingertip to trick the brain into feeling friction. When the wheel spins faster or slower than expected relative to movement, virtual gobs of honey or oil feel remarkably tactile.

t: What’s new in Microsoft Foundry
r: As agentic workflows become standard enterprise architecture, moving from debugging a trace to testing a fix needs tighter integration. Microsoft's latest updates connect diagnostic insights directly to agent optimization and continuous evaluation tools.
s: Microsoft Foundry's latest preview features tie runtime insights directly to its Agent Optimizer, helping developers turn trace failures into tested fixes. The updates bring continuous improvement tools and multi-turn evaluation capabilities into standard agent development pipelines.

t: Is “sort by impact” just vibes?
r: When developers ask AI agents to sort backlogs by impact without defining the metric, it's easy to assume the model is just guessing based on tone. A new study by Microsoft developers reveals a surprising consistency across models, even if the underlying definition remains implicit.
s: Testing how AI agents rank items by vague criteria like impact, researchers found that different models largely agreed with each other across thousands of runs. Even without explicit definitions for impact, the agents converged on remarkably consistent prioritization orders.

t: Eye of the Sahara
r: Orbital photography offers breathtaking perspectives on terrestrial geology that ground-level views simply cannot match. This crisp shot of the Richat Structure from the International Space Station highlights millions of years of geological uplift and erosion in stunning detail.
s: Captured from the International Space Station, the Richat Structure in Mauritania displays its massive concentric rings in striking clarity. Known as the Eye of the Sahara, the 45-kilometer-wide geological dome was shaped by ancient igneous activity and differential rock erosion.

t: The Physics Wall Facing Orbital AI Data Centers
r: While tech companies frequently tout the boundless energy of space for orbital AI data centers, a new preprint paper highlights the harsh physical constraints that make such ambitions impractical for the foreseeable future. Grounded engineering analysis offers a refreshing dose of reality against speculative industry hype.
s: A new paper by Dr. Slava Turyshev of NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory examines the physical hurdles facing orbital AI data centers. While the math might look good on paper, utilizing the Sun's free energy and processing power in space involves prohibitive constraints that will take a long time to overcome.

t: Novel Experiments Expand the Hunt for ‘Ultralight’ Dark Matter
r: Dark matter remains one of the most compelling mysteries in modern astrophysics, and expanding the search into ultralight candidates showcases the clever experimental setups physicists use to probe the unseen universe.
s: Nearly a century after Fritz Zwicky and Vera Rubin established the case for dark matter, modern researchers are deploying novel experimental approaches to hunt for hypothetical ultralight dark matter particles, continuing our quest to understand what makes up the vast majority of the cosmos.

t: The Curious Case of the Second Spacebar
r: Hardware modding stories from decades past provide a wonderful window into how early computer hobbyists adapted their machines before standard peripherals settled into today's uniform layouts.
s: A retrocomputing enthusiast recently investigated a heavily modified Commodore 64 featuring both an unexplained DIP socket and a mysterious second spacebar above the number row. Reverse engineering revealed the modifications served as a makeshift numeric keypad port and an extra shift key for quick symbol entry.

t: AI is Changing the Cross-Platform Decision Matrix
r: Software engineering decisions have historically been bound by team size, knowledge, and maintenance costs. Factoring AI coding assistants into that matrix changes the calculus for cross-platform app development in meaningful ways.
s: The factors guiding cross-platform app development decisions—such as team capacity, tech stack familiarity, and maintenance overhead—are evolving. With well-configured AI coding tools and assistants becoming standard parts of the workflow, traditional team knowledge constraints look quite different.

t: ALMA Reveals a Dying Star's Final Breath, Encoded In a Giant Ring of Gas
r: Observational astronomy that captures the intricate final stages of stellar evolution offers stunning physical evidence for theoretical models of dying stars.
s: Using the ALMA observatory, astronomers have detected a giant ring of gas emitted during a thermal pulse by a dying star 6,500 years ago. This observation provides the first direct evidence supporting theoretical predictions about how these stellar remnants form complex nebulae.

t: The Hidden Spiegeltent in Chicago, Illinois
r: Overlooked historical spaces tucked away inside modern or repurposed buildings offer a fascinating glimpse into urban architectural oddities and past eras of entertainment.
s: While traditional Spiegeltents were designed as portable wooden dance halls, the example tucked away on the 14th floor of a Chicago building was constructed entirely indoors in 1926. Originally built as a Masonic hall above a movie palace, it stands as a unique indoor relic of another era.

t: Sodium Vapor Around Europa Hints at Its Hidden Ocean
r: Planetary science breakthroughs that connect observable atmospheric phenomena to subsurface oceans are vital for understanding Jovian moons. Astronomers have found a stable cloud of sodium vapor around Europa that originates directly from its interior ocean.
s: Observations indicate that a steady cloud of sodium vapor surrounding Jupiter's moon Europa likely traces its source back to the moon's subsurface ocean.

t: DocumentExtractionClient Preview Brings Unified Document Parsing to .NET
r: Extracting structured data from PDFs, invoices, and office files is a standard requirement for modern enterprise applications and AI context pipelines. The new preview of DocumentExtractionClient in Microsoft.Extensions.DocumentExtraction provides a standardized approach rather than forcing developers to use disparate SDKs.
s: A new .NET preview package offers a unified client interface to extract content and structure from documents like PDFs, scans, and office files for downstream apps and AI models.

t: The Emergence of Dark Nebula Lynds 1251
o: NASA Astronomy Picture of the Day
r: Deep-sky astrophotography often reveals complex dust clouds that remain hidden to casual observation. This stunning capture of dark nebula Lynds 1251 highlights how long exposure times bring out obscured cosmic structures.
s: An astrophotography capture reveals the intricate dust lanes and emerging star-forming regions of the dark nebula Lynds 1251.

t: Designing a Passively Morphing Quadcopter for Narrow Gaps
r: Engineering reliable robotic hardware without adding excessive mechanical complexity is a perpetual challenge in drone design. Researchers have demonstrated a quadcopter that uses flexible elastic rolling cam joints to passively fold its arms when encountering obstacles.
s: Engineers built a quadcopter with flexible joints that allows the frame to passively morph and squeeze through narrow gaps before snapping back into place.

t: Air Force Deploys New System to Warn of Solar Disruptions in Space
r: Space weather monitoring is increasingly critical for protecting operational satellites and ground infrastructure from geomagnetic activity. New early warning systems enhance our ability to track solar disruptions before they impact orbital assets.
s: Military and meteorological authorities have deployed new early warning infrastructure to monitor solar disruptions and protect space assets from space weather impacts.

t: Discovering the World's Only Dinosaur Pulpit in Thailand
r: Local history and peculiar architectural quirks make for delightful cultural discoveries outside mainstream tech. A Buddhist temple in Thailand features a pulpit uniquely styled around dinosaur fossils discovered in the region.
s: A temple in Thailand's Isan region houses a one-of-a-kind pulpit adorned with dinosaur motifs, nodding to the area's history as the site of the country's first fossil finds.

t: Minnesota Officials Urge Ice Safety Awareness as Cold Weather Approaches
r: Early winter safety warnings are an essential seasonal ritual for outdoor enthusiasts across Minnesota. Local authorities are reminding parents and residents to talk about ice safety before early-season freezes prove dangerous.
s: Minnesota safety officials are urging parents and communities to discuss ice safety with children as early winter temperatures begin to settle across the region.

t: Space Lasers Are Fast, But Clouds Still Rule the Forecast
r: Infrared laser communications promise incredible bandwidth upgrades for deep-space and orbital networking compared to congested radio waves. However, atmospheric physics and cloud cover still impose stubborn constraints on ground stations. It's a fascinating look at the engineering tradeoffs between raw speed and terrestrial weather.
s: While optical laser links offer massive data transfer rates for spacecraft communications, pre-print research highlights how atmospheric interference and clouds continue to pose significant operational challenges for ground-based receivers.

t: Troubleshooting Ethernet Networks with the ESP32
r: Diagnosing live TCP/IP networks and flaky physical links usually requires lugging around a bulky laptop or expensive specialized testers. Turning a cheap microcontroller development board into a self-contained diagnostic tool is classic hardware hacking ingenuity. Any developer who has crawled under a desk will appreciate this compact build.
s: A clever open-source firmware project transforms an ESP32 development board into a pocket-sized Ethernet tester capable of checking link status, pinging IP addresses, detecting LLDP devices, and inspecting DHCP services.

t: New Research Reveals Europa's Sodium Cloud Originated from its Interior Ocean
r: Understanding the composition of icy moons gives planetary scientists critical clues about subsurface oceans and potential habitability without needing to drill through kilometers of ice. This spectroscopic observation connects surface phenomena directly to internal water bodies. It's a brilliant example of remote planetary analysis.
s: Using the W.M. Keck Observatory's HIRISE spectrometer, researchers have traced the origin of Europa's sodium cloud back to its subsurface interior ocean, offering new insights into the moon's internal chemistry.

t: NASA Seeks Partners to Design First Nuclear Reactor for the Moon
r: Solar power alone cannot reliably sustain a permanent lunar base through the long, dark lunar nights, making small fission reactors a critical engineering necessity. NASA's push for a 20-kilowatt system moves lunar habitation one step closer to reality. It's a major milestone for off-world energy infrastructure.
s: NASA is soliciting industry proposals to develop Lunar Reactor-1, a compact 20-kilowatt fission power system intended to supply continuous electricity for future long-duration human habitats and scientific equipment on the Moon.

t: Making Sense of Chaotic Supernova Ejecta With the JWST
r: Stars keep their secrets close until they explode, scattering their insides across the cosmos where astronomers can finally examine them. The James Webb Space Telescope provides a remarkably detailed look at these messy stellar remains, helping researchers piece together how stars live and die. It is a fantastic reminder of how violent cosmic events fuel our understanding of the universe.
s: Although it is impossible to look inside an active star, exploding stars spread their material outward for detailed examination. Astronomers are using the JWST as a stellar forensics tool to make sense of chaotic supernova ejecta.

t: Run local models in your .NET apps with Llama on Windows
r: Running AI models locally has traditionally required a mountain of specialized configuration and command-line setup. Llama on Windows bridges that gap by providing a simple tray app to manage downloads and local execution. Best of all, it opens the door for .NET 11 C# file-based applications to talk directly to local models without paying per request.
s: A new tray app called Llama on Windows makes it easy to find, download, and run open models locally on your PC. Once running, .NET apps can seamlessly communicate with the local server to handle queries offline.

t: Ultra-Thin "Rainbow" Sails Could Power Spacecraft and Shade the Earth
r: Solar sailing relies on the gentle momentum of photons bouncing off reflective surfaces to push spacecraft through the void. A new preprint paper from Rochester Institute of Technology researchers proposes an ingenious design using ultra-thin rainbow sails capable of sideways steering. If scaled up, these clever sails could even help shade the Earth.
s: Researchers have unveiled a novel solar sail design that uses light momentum and specialized optical properties to steer sideways. The concept offers exciting possibilities for both propulsion and planetary-scale shading.

t: Building a wireless network adapter for the Super Nintendo
r: Retrofitting networking onto a 16-bit console built in 1990 is the ultimate hacker project. By tapping into the front serial controller ports, this project connects an RP2350 and an ESP32-C3 to bridge vintage hardware with modern WebDAV servers and LLM-generated dialogue. It is a delightful blend of retrocomputing nostalgia and modern engineering.
s: A new hardware project adds wireless networking to the Super Nintendo by interfacing with its controller ports. The adapter pairs an RP2350 with an ESP32-C3, allowing patched ROMs to sync game saves and even generate dynamic NPC text.

t: LISA's Gravitational Wave Detections Could Reveal Exoplanets
r: The upcoming Laser Interferometry Space Antenna is designed to catch gravitational waves from massive merging objects far across the universe. New research demonstrates that exoplanets orbiting those systems leave subtle, detectable signatures in the ripples of spacetime. It is a brilliant example of how next-generation observatories will uncover hidden worlds.
s: ESA's upcoming LISA gravitational wave observatory might be able to spot exoplanets through the tiny gravitational tugs they exert on merging massive objects. Researchers show that these planetary influences leave a measurable trace on spacetime ripples.

t: NASA’s Webb Shows How Supernova Dust Chronicles Star Evolution
r: Supernova remnants like Cassiopeia A are treasure troves of astrophysical data, preserving the history of ancient stars in their expanding clouds. The James Webb Space Telescope has captured vibrant new imagery of the hot dust within the remnant. This data provides crucial clues regarding the structure and composition of the original star.
s: NASA's James Webb Space Telescope has imaged the hot dust inside the Cassiopeia A supernova remnant. The detailed composition of the dust offers new clues into the structure and life cycle of the star that formed it.

t: Euclid's Hunt for Strong Gravitational Lenses is Off to a Strong Start
r: The Euclid space telescope has quickly cataloged 15,000 strong gravitational lens candidates in its initial data release. These natural cosmic lenses are critical probes for mapping dark matter and understanding the expansion history of the universe.
s: The Euclid space telescope is off to a remarkably productive start in its mission to map cosmic structure, identifying 15,000 strong gravitational lens candidates in its first data release. These massive structures bend light from distant galaxies, providing astronomers with powerful tools to study dark matter.

t: November 2026 Night Sky: What to See
r: November brings an exceptional lineup for observers and astrophotographers, featuring meteor showers, planetary conjunctions, and Uranus at opposition. Practical astronomical guides help backyard observers plan their imaging sessions around optimal lunar phases.
s: November 2026 offers a rich selection of astronomical observing targets, including the Taurid and Leonid meteor showers, a tight conjunction of Mars and Jupiter, and Uranus reaching opposition. Stargazers can also catch the full Beaver Supermoon while taking advantage of longer autumn nights.

t: EF-1 tornado confirmed in Palm Beach County during Saturday storms
r: Regional severe weather events provide important case studies for local meteorology and radar tracking. Confirming damage paths helps researchers correlate Doppler signatures with ground truth.
s: National Weather Service meteorologists have confirmed an EF-1 tornado touched down in Palm Beach County during a round of severe Saturday storms. The twister caused localized property damage, downed trees, and prompted multiple tornado warnings across South Florida.

t: Hosted agents in your own virtual network: five checks when the Agents page times out
r: Deploying hosted AI agents inside locked-down virtual networks frequently leads to subtle routing and DNS configuration traps. This troubleshooting checklist walks through the exact diagnostic commands needed when private endpoints and firewalls block traffic.
s: Moving hosted AI agents into a spoke virtual network with strict outbound inspection and private endpoints often results in initialization timeouts. This troubleshooting guide provides five targeted checks to isolate DNS and routing issues when agent management pages fail to load.

t: Serve open models in production with Foundry Managed Compute
r: Managing open-source model runtimes in production requires balancing GPU provisioning, container lifecycles, and regional scaling constraints. General availability announcements like this highlight how cloud platforms are streamlining deployment pipelines for custom AI models.
s: Microsoft has announced the general availability of Managed Compute in Microsoft Foundry, designed to simplify serving open-source models in production. The service handles GPU provisioning, runtime containers, and deployment scaling across multiple data zones.

t: NASA Science Data Powers New Method to Discover Hard-to-Find Pulsars
r: A million-fold speedup in finding pulsars opens up a massive trove of discovery in existing space telescope archives. It is a fantastic example of open science tooling unlocking hidden needles in cosmic haystacks.
s: An international team of scientists has developed a new method using 15 years of publicly available data from NASA's Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope to find pulsars about a million times faster than before. The technique promises to accelerate the discovery of rapidly spinning cores of dead stars across the sky.

t: ESA's Hera Probe Uses 'Superhuman' Vision to Inspect NASA's Asteroid Crash Site
r: Four years after DART smashed into Dimorphos, the European Space Agency's Hera probe has arrived to examine the aftermath up close. It is a wonderful follow-up to humanity's first kinetic impact test.
s: The European Space Agency's Hera probe has arrived at the binary asteroid system targeted by NASA's DART mission four years ago. Hera is now using advanced imaging to inspect the asteroid crash site and measure the true structural results of the intentional impact.

t: A Replacement PCB for the Echo Dot Pushes the ESP32-P4 Forward
r: Gutting a commercial smart speaker to run entirely on local hardware with Home Assistant is pure maker gold. It also highlights practical uses for newer microcontrollers like the ESP32-P4.
s: Maker ale1800 gutted a third-generation Amazon Echo Dot and replaced its internal board with a custom PCB powered by an ESP32-P4 application processor and ESP32-S3 connectivity. The modified device retains the original microphone array while routing voice commands exclusively through a local Home Assistant server.

t: Azure Cobalt 200 VMs Now Available for Agentic Workloads
r: Arm-based cloud infrastructure continues to mature, with custom silicon specifically optimized for the heavy demands of modern multi-agent cloud workflows. It's a solid look at what's running underneath modern enterprise software stacks.
s: Microsoft announced the general availability of Azure Cobalt 200-based virtual machines, promising up to 50 percent better performance than their predecessors. The new ARM-based instances are tailored for data-intensive and agentic AI workloads across multiple cloud regions.

t: Study Reveals How 2024 Geomagnetic Storm Created Unprecedented Four Electron Bands
r: Major geomagnetic storms continue to reveal surprising dynamics in Earth's radiation belts. Understanding how extreme space weather reconfigures the Van Allen belts helps protect operational satellites.
s: Recent analysis of the intense 2024 geomagnetic storm has revealed that the severe space weather event created an unprecedented four distinct electron bands within Earth's Van Allen radiation belts. The findings give scientists new insight into how planetary magnetospheres react to massive solar outbursts.

t: NWS Confirms Saturday Evening Tornado in Palm Beach County
r: Severe weather reports from late November serve as a stark reminder of how unstable atmospheric conditions can spin up unseasonal tornadoes outside traditional peak regions.
s: The National Weather Service confirmed that a tornado touched down in Palm Beach County on Saturday evening, prompting multiple warnings across South Florida. Local residents surveyed structural damage and reported high winds as the weather system moved through the region.

t: Soft Robot Powered by Pneumatic Logic Sets Speed Landmark
r: Achieving higher land speeds in soft robotics without relying on a traditional onboard microcontroller is a neat engineering breakthrough. Pneumatic logic gates offer a fascinating alternative actuation method.
s: Researchers at UC San Diego have set a new speed milestone for soft robotics using an entirely 3D-printed design that relies on pneumatic logic gates rather than a direct microcontroller. The embedded fluidic pathways allow for rapid oscillations and quick cycling of its soft actuators.

t: The Hunger Games Prequel Explores the Arena Through Haymitch's Eyes
r: Franchise expansions often lean hard into familiar tropes, making critical breakdowns of adaptation choices a fun read for sci-fi fans tracking modern cinematic world-building.
s: Recent analysis of the expanding Hunger Games cinematic universe examines how prequel storytelling handles established characters like Haymitch Abernathy. The adaptation choices continue to lean into clear depictions of arena brutality while navigating the weight of past lore.

t: Swirls and Colors on Jupiter from Juno
r: NASA's Juno spacecraft continues to provide breathtaking views of Jupiter's complex cloud tops. Even with decades of observation, the exact trace molecules responsible for the vibrant color bands in the hydrogen and helium atmosphere remain an active area of research.
s: A stunning new image from the Juno spacecraft highlights the colorful swirls and cloud formations of Jupiter. While the giant planet's atmosphere is mostly colorless hydrogen and helium at low temperatures, researchers continue to study which trace molecules create its distinct hues.

t: Building a Robotic Hand on a Budget
d: from the servo and tendon dept.
r: Dexterity in robotics is notoriously difficult and expensive to achieve, making this sub-$300 eighteen-degree-of-freedom hand a fascinating hardware project. Utilizing 3D-printed skeletons and thin steel rope instead of synthetic fiber cables provides clever engineering solutions for makers.
s: A builder has designed an 18-degree-of-freedom robot hand and forearm for under $300 in parts. The design uses 3D-printed components, servo motors in the forearm, and thin steel rope running through PTFE tubing to actuate joints without tricky knots.

t: Potatoes Grow in Simulated Lunar Soil as Well as on Earth
r: Testing whether crops can thrive in lunar regolith simulants is an essential step for future crewed bases on the Moon. Oregon State University researchers evaluated not just growth, but nutritional value and absorbed metals in these harsh conditions.
s: Researchers at Oregon State University have successfully grown potatoes in lunar regolith simulants, analyzing both crop yield and nutritional value. As expected for nutrient-poor regolith, adding fertilizer significantly improved growth, providing practical data for future lunar habitats.

t: Tornado Touches Down Near Delray Beach, Leaving Damage Behind
d: from the radar and warning dept.
r: The National Weather Service confirmed a late-season tornado in South Florida that left behind structural damage in local neighborhoods. Severe weather reports of this nature highlight the localized intensity of unexpected atmospheric disturbances.
s: A confirmed tornado touched down near Delray Beach in Palm Beach County, bringing high winds and causing reported property damage in the area. The National Weather Service tracked the system through multiple local warning offices before the threat subsided.

t: Xingyun Awards 2026 Winners Announced
r: Tracking major international science fiction awards highlights prominent works and translations shaping the genre globally. The World Chinese Science Fiction Association recently announced its latest slate of winners in Chengdu.
s: The 17th annual Xingyun Awards for Chinese science fiction were announced by the World Chinese Science Fiction Association during a ceremony in Chengdu. The awards recognized top achievements across novels, novellas, short stories, and translated works.

t: The Stormy Southwest Pacific
r: While the North Atlantic hurricane season wound down quietly, activity in the Southern Hemisphere picked up sharply. The rapid intensification of tropical cyclone Xavier provides a textbook look at regional storm dynamics.
s: As the Atlantic storm season winds down, the Southwest Pacific has seen severe weather stir with the rapid intensification of a tropical system named Xavier. The Fiji Meteorological Service tracked the slow-moving disturbance as it quickly grew into a powerful November tropical cyclone.

t: ESP32 Drives Vintage MDA Monochrome Display for Wireless Terminal
r: This delightful hardware-software hack bridges modern microcontrollers with ancient display tech. It shows how oscilloscope timing and custom terminal firmware can bring classic green-and-amber iron back to life.
s: An ESP32 development board has been programmed to drive a Monochrome Display Adapter monitor, complete with custom VGA-to-TTL timing. The setup runs a retro command-line interface styled like IBM OfficeVision, serving as both a word processor and a media server controller.

t: A Radical Theory About a 26.7-Billion-Year-Old Universe Passes Key Tests
r: Alternative cosmological models that challenge the standard Lambda-CDM paradigm are always worth watching when they face rigorous testing. This University of Ottawa study explores a universe that requires neither dark matter nor dark energy.
s: A bold alternative model proposing a 26.7-billion-year-old universe has held up against several major cosmology tests. The hypothesis dispenses with the need for dark matter and dark energy, offering a fresh perspective on cosmic evolution.

t: Astronomers Watch One Star Swallow Another in Real Time
r: Catching a stellar merger in progress is an extraordinary astronomical observation that illuminates the violent life cycles of binary systems. This multi-year study captures the exact infall of a star spiraling into its giant companion's core.
s: For the first time, astronomers have documented the multi-year infall of a star spiraling into a giant stellar companion. The observations culminated in the smaller star splashing directly into the core of its host.

t: Open-Source Swimming Pool Automation Controller Built on ESP32-S3
r: Practical home automation projects that solve messy physical maintenance problems with microcontroller logic are a joy to examine. This open-source design monitors water chemistry and pump safety without proprietary lock-in.
s: The Swimming Pool System Open (SPSO) project uses an ESP32-S3 microcontroller to monitor pH, chlorine, temperature, and filter pressure. It automatically controls chemical dosing and filtration pumps while integrating neatly with Home Assistant.

t: Custom Firmware Unlocks Advanced RF and Ham Radio Features on Communication Analyzers
r: Unlocking specialized test equipment with community-built firmware demonstrates deep engineering reverse-engineering skill. It turns expensive lab gear into an even more versatile tool for radio enthusiasts.
s: Developer [iu2frl] has created custom firmware for Rhode & Schwarz CMU200 and CMU300 communication analyzers. The upgrade adds a tracking generator, WFM reception with RDS decoding, amateur radio test suites, and remote control via FTP, VNC, and HTTP servers.

t: Open-Source HDMI-to-CSI Bridge Boards Bring Clean Video Capture to SBCs
r: Converting HDMI inputs directly into camera serial interfaces opens up fantastic possibilities for custom KVMs and embedded video projects. Releasing open-source hardware designs for multiple single-board computers is a great boon for builders.
s: The WarpKVM team has released open-source CERN OHL board designs that convert HDMI signals into CSI camera interfaces. Tailored for popular single-board computers, the hardware supports 4K at 30 FPS and 1080p at 120 FPS for digital video capture.

t: Manganese Alloying Addresses Durability Challenges in Aluminum Anode Batteries
r: Improving metal alloy anodes for lithium-ion batteries is crucial for pushing energy density and charge rates forward. Addressing volumetric expansion through manganese alloying represents a clever metallurgical fix to a stubborn chemical problem.
s: Researchers have found that alloying aluminum battery anodes with manganese can prevent lithium from getting trapped beneath cracked, delithiated surfaces. This approach tackles the durability challenges of volumetric expansion, paving the way for higher-capacity metal alloy batteries.

t: BepiColombo Arrives at Mercury After 8-Year Odyssey
r: After an eight-year journey filled with gravity assists, twin orbiters from Europe and Japan have finally reached Mercury to unlock its planetary secrets. Interplanetary rendezvous of this complexity represent monumental feats of orbital mechanics and international cooperation.
s: Europe and Japan's joint BepiColombo mission successfully arrived at Mercury on November 21st, beginning its long-awaited orbital exploration of the innermost planet.

t: A Triple Star System 'That Shouldn't Exist,' Only 28 Light-Years from Earth
r: Discovering astronomical systems that defy current models of stellar evolution is what keeps astrophysics thrilling. Finding such an oddity right in our local galactic neighborhood makes it even better.
s: Astronomers have identified a triple star system only 28 light-years away that defies standard models of stellar evolution and common envelopes, existing despite theoretical odds.

t: A Medium-Sized Solar Flare
o: NASA Astronomy Picture of the Day
r: Combining exposures of the solar chromosphere over a ten-minute window reveals the dynamic thermal layers of our nearest star. It is a stunning visual reminder of how active our Sun remains day-to-day.
s: Astrophotographer Mario Cogo captured a medium-sized solar flare using specialized techniques to reveal the Sun's chromosphere and the magnetic heating mechanisms above its surface.

t: Multiple Wavelengths Of Sun Blasts X1.2-Class Solar Flare
r: Major flare activity captured across multiple wavelengths provides researchers with critical data on high-energy solar events. Keeping an eye on X-class eruptions is essential for understanding real-world space weather impacts.
s: The Sun recently blasted an X1.2-class solar flare observed across multiple wavelengths, highlighting ongoing space weather dynamics.

t: Complex Life on Earth May Not Have Appeared Without Tall Mountains
r: Linking planetary geomorphology directly to the rise of atmospheric oxygen and complex life connects geology with astrobiology in a fascinating way. It provides fresh context for what makes an exoplanet truly habitable.
s: New research suggests that ancient mountain-building spurts washed vital nutrients into early oceans, driving oxygenation events that made complex life on Earth possible.

t: Printable Homelab Racks You Can Design In A Browser
r: For anyone drowning in small single-board computers, switches, and tangled cables, a browser-based tool to plan 3D-printable racks is immensely practical. It bridges digital design with physical homelab organization.
s: A new browser-based tool called Printable Racks allows makers to design and test fits for custom 10-inch hardware enclosures using a catalog of hundreds of 3D-printable components.

t: Curiosity Spots Drifting Twilight Clouds on Mars
r: Observing seasonal weather patterns on another planet gives planetary scientists valuable comparative data on atmospheric dynamics. It's a wonderful reminder of how dynamic neighboring worlds really are.
s: NASA's Curiosity rover has captured drifting post-sunset twilight clouds over Gale Crater during its ongoing Martian exploration. These delicate clouds appear briefly each fall and are documented using the rover's navigation cameras.

t: Exploring the Prehistoric Rock Carvings of Alta, Norway
r: Ancient rock art offers a direct physical window into the lives and observations of prehistoric humans millennia ago. It's fascinating to see how geological uplift has preserved these ancient galleries along rising coastlines.
s: Thousands of original prehistoric artworks carved directly into bedrock can be found at Alta Museum's outdoor site in northern Norway. Dating back over 7,000 years, these ancient petroglyphs depict wildlife, hunting scenes, and rituals along what was once an ancient shoreline.

t: Breathing New Life Into an Old FireWire Audio Interface with USB-C
r: Rescuing capable legacy hardware from planned obsolescence is an endlessly satisfying engineering exercise. This project demonstrates clever reverse engineering and practical circuit modification.
s: A resourceful hacker successfully modernized a classic PreSonus Firestudio Project audio interface by replacing its obsolete FireWire controller with an XMOS-based USB audio setup. By carefully tracing digital audio signals and maintaining equal-length conductors, the project brings eight inputs and outputs to modern machines.

t: Sound Waves from Sunspots Launch Plasma Jets Across the Sun
r: Understanding the mechanisms behind coronal heating remains one of solar physics' most compelling challenges. Tracking these dynamic fibrils brings us one step closer to explaining our star's extreme outer temperatures.
s: New research published in The Astrophysical Journal details the tracking of roughly two hundred dynamic fibrils—jet-like bursts of plasma launched from the Sun's surface. These observations help solve the enduring mystery of why the Sun's outer atmosphere is hundreds of times hotter than its core.

t: Morse Code Message Shines into the Night Sky for Voyager 1
r: Blending amateur astronomy techniques with a tribute to humanity's most distant emissary makes for a delightful astrophotography project. It highlights both technical creativity and enduring cosmic curiosity.
s: Observers at the Emirates Astronomical Observatory used a flashlight beam to trace a Morse code call sign into a time-exposure night sky photo. The message spelled 'V-G-R' to honor fans of interstellar spaceflight and the distant Voyager 1 spacecraft.

t: Astronomers Watch a Stellar Merger in Real Time
r: Witnessing a binary star system spiral together and create a luminous red nova gives astrophysicists a front-row seat to stellar evolution in action. It is a fantastic piece of observational astronomy that turns abstract theory into real-time discovery.
s: When a primary star draws material away from its companion, the shared envelope exerts drag, causing the two stars to spiral inward. For the very first time, astronomers have observed this catastrophic stellar merger as it happened, offering new clues into the formation of luminous red novas.

t: Tiny Grains of Sand Reveal Wind Speeds on Alien Worlds
r: Planetary scientists have long used dune orientation as a weather vane, but figuring out wind velocity has remained tricky. This new research adds a clever mechanical dimension to planetary science using basic sand grains.
s: Scientists have determined that the size and orientation of sand dunes across the solar system can act as cosmic speedometers. Researchers at Stanford showed that dune morphology can reveal how fast alien winds are blowing, solving a long-standing riddle in planetary meteorology.

t: Repurposing E-Paper Price Tags Into Miniature Desktop Picture Frames
d: from the electronic shelf label hacks dept.
r: Hacking commodity hardware with custom firmware always makes for a satisfying project. This work transforms mundane retail displays into charming, low-power browser-connected photo frames.
s: Electronic shelf labels are finding a second life thanks to open firmware projects like pin16. By flashing Solum e-paper price tags over a debug interface, makers can push custom four-color images via Bluetooth to build tiny, battery-efficient slideshow frames.

t: A Browser Game Where You Compete by Crashing Real Microcontrollers
d: from the distributed hardware abuse dept.
r: Combining web applications with physical microcontroller stress tests is delightfully unhinged engineering. It turns server overload into an interactive, chaotic multiplayer sport.
s: A new browser-based game pits players against each other in a race to secure festival toilets by digitally knocking on their doors. Each virtual knock increases the computational load on a real-world ESP8266 microcontroller until it runs out of memory, crashes, and reboots.

t: Relentless Atmospheric River Smashes Decades-Old Rainfall Records in California
r: Tracking major meteorological extremes provides valuable context on moisture transport without getting bogged down in routine forecasts or climate policy shouting matches.
s: A punishing succession of atmospheric rivers has lashed California, dumping heavy snow in the mountains and flooding urban centers like San Francisco's Financial District. The storm system shattered rainfall records that had stood for 76 years.

t: The Glacial Plumbing Behind Maine's Thundering Coastal Cavern
r: Understanding the physical forces that turn ancient glacial fissures into roaring tourist attractions marries geology with pure acoustic wonder.
s: Acadia National Park's Thunder Hole is a natural geological formation created by thousands of years of glacial activity. As high tide forces waves into a narrow granite channel and a submerged cavern, the compressed air produces a booming roar and massive water sprays.

t: The Wachowskis Formally Exercise Copyright Termination to Reclaim The Matrix
d: from the cyberpunk IP reclamation dept.
r: Copyright termination clauses offer a fascinating legal mechanism for creators to take back their foundational works after three decades. It is a notable milestone for science fiction film history.
s: Filmmakers Lana and Lilly Wachowski have notified Warner Bros. that they are exercising their copyright termination rights under U.S. law. The move could allow the creative team behind The Matrix to reclaim rights to the iconic franchise by February 2029.

t: El Niño Rains Transform the Arid Atacama Desert
r: Following an unusually wet winter in late 2026, satellite imaging captures rare, widespread blooming across parts of the Atacama Desert normally known as one of the driest places on Earth. It is a striking look at how climate cycles awaken dormant seeds on a massive scale.
s: Landsat data reveals vibrant bands of red-purple, green, and white across northern Chile's Atacama Desert following heavy El Niño rains. The moisture triggered what scientists suspect is one of the most extensive desert blooms in recent years.

t: Computer Simulations Explain James Webb's 'Little Red Dots'
r: The mysterious compact red galaxies spotted by the James Webb Space Telescope have puzzled astronomers since their discovery. New computer models offer a compelling explanation, suggesting they are the remnants of massive primordial stars.
s: Researchers using advanced computer simulations have found that the enigmatic 'Little Red Dot' galaxies discovered by JWST are likely the remains of supermassive primordial stars shrouded in dense gaseous envelopes.

t: Handheld Brushless Motor Gimbal Cancels Motion in Real-Time
r: Combining a tiny STM32 microcontroller board with a brushless motor creates an impressive one-axis gimbal that stabilizes against physical twists in real time. It is a neat hardware project that demonstrates the responsiveness of tight control loops.
s: A developer built a compact handheld gimbal using an STM32-based microcontroller and a brushless motor with a CAN interface. The device tracks motion across three dimensions and actively compensates for disturbances within a fraction of a rotation.

t: How Hough Transforms Help Computers See Lines in Noise
r: Understanding the foundational algorithms behind computer vision is always worthwhile for software engineers. This deep dive looks at how Paul Hough's 1960s feature extraction method evolved from bubble chamber particle tracking into modern automated line detection.
s: A detailed technical video explores the Hough Transform, an edge-detection and feature-extraction algorithm originally developed for analyzing bubble chamber photographs. The piece breaks down how mathematical transformations allow computer vision systems to pick out patterns from complex visual scenes.

t: Atmospheric River Lashes California with Record Rainfall
r: Major moisture plumes consistently test regional infrastructure and forecasting precision along the West Coast. This storm system brought notable precipitation totals and rare tornado warnings to parts of the San Francisco Bay area.
s: A potent atmospheric river swept across California's Bay Area, delivering record-breaking rainfall and gusty winds. The severe weather prompted local emergency responses and rare tornado alerts along the coast.

t: NASA Launches Mid-Power Electric Rocket Challenge for U.S. Firms
r: Hall effect thrusters offer immense efficiency gains over chemical rockets for long-duration space missions. NASA's new competition aims to push commercial prototyping forward for future deep-space and satellite operations.
s: NASA has initiated a new challenge inviting domestic companies to design mid-power Hall effect thruster prototypes. These electric propulsion systems use magnetic and electric fields to accelerate propellant gas, achieving far greater efficiency than standard chemical rockets.

t: Microsoft Announces Enterprise Context Platform Microsoft IQ
r: As agentic systems become more prevalent, managing proprietary organizational context securely across multi-agent workflows is a critical infrastructure challenge. This Ignite 2026 announcement introduces a platform specifically designed to feed institutional data into AI models safely.
s: At Microsoft Ignite, the company introduced Microsoft IQ, an enterprise context management platform designed to integrate organizational data, communications, and workflows into AI agents. The system aims to ground foundational models in proprietary corporate intelligence.

t: APOD: The Horsehead and Flame Nebulas
r: A stunning look at the iconic Orion Belt region featuring blue Alnitak and the famous dark dust cloud. It's a gorgeous reminder of the complex chemistry sculpting our galaxy.
s: Today's Astronomy Picture of the Day highlights the Horsehead and Flame Nebulas, showcasing the brilliant blue triple star Alnitak alongside intricate dark molecular clouds.

t: Are Uranus and Neptune Secretly 'Rock Giants'?
d: from the ice giant interior dept.
r: Investigating whether our solar system's ice giants actually harbor massive rocky cores beneath their crushing atmospheres helps refine planetary formation models.
s: A new paper suggests that measuring isotopes of noble gases like argon-40 could reveal whether Uranus and Neptune contain hidden mountains of rock deep beneath their thick mantles.

t: Coronal Hole and CME Combo Threatens Mid-Latitude Aurora
r: Combining coronal hole streams with coronal mass ejections frequently delivers fantastic high-latitude and mid-latitude auroral displays for backyard observers.
s: Forecasters report that a combined coronal hole and CME solar driver could trigger visible northern light displays across parts of the United States.

r: Unusual meteorological events like bay waterspouts underscore the intense localized impact active El Niño moisture plumes bring to coastal regions.
s: Rare waterspouts formed over the San Francisco Bay as a potent atmospheric river fueled heavy downpours and stormy conditions across Northern California.

t: Mesh2Cad Automates the Pain of Re-Modelling STLs
r: Converting messy polygon meshes into clean, parametric CAD files is a universal headache for makers and engineers trying to modify existing prints.
s: A new open-source Python tool called Mesh2Cad translates 3D meshes into parametric formats compatible with FreeCAD, STEP, and OpenSCAD by approximating geometries within user-defined tolerances.

t: Microsoft Ignite 2026 Spotlights AI-Driven Azure Infrastructure
r: As agentic workloads demand more from hardware and databases, announcements around custom silicon like Cobalt 200 VMs show how cloud platforms are adapting.
s: Microsoft's Ignite conference rolled out major updates for Azure, including general availability for high-performance Cobalt 200 virtual machines, new PostgreSQL database engines for AI, and agentic orchestration tools.

t: Wax: Revisit the 1991 Beekeeping Art Film That Streamed Early
r: Looking back at David Blair's experimental cyber-film offers a fascinating glimpse into early digital art and pre-web streaming culture.
s: David Blair's experimental 1991 film 'Wax, or the Discovery of Television Among the Bees' combined early computer graphics and nonlinear storytelling in a pioneering digital broadcast.

t: Binh Lam Champa Tower Rises from Vietnamese Lowlands
r: Most ancient Cham towers perch on dramatic hills, making this lowland brick sanctuary with hidden subterranean archaeology a unique architectural puzzle.
s: Constructed between the late tenth and eleventh centuries, the 20-meter Binh Lam Tower in Vietnam serves as an architectural bridge featuring subtle vertical pilasters and hidden subterranean ruins.

t: Fermi’s 14-Year All-Sky Map Bridges Astronomy’s Elusive 'MeV Gap'
r: Gamma-ray astronomy has wrestled with the 'MeV gap' blind spot for decades, making this all-sky map a stellar milestone. It highlights how the Fermi Large Area Telescope collaboration successfully pinned down hundreds of low-energy gamma-ray sources.
s: An international group of scientists using data from the Fermi Large Area Telescope collaboration has mapped 450 cosmic sources in the 20-200 mega-electron volt range. This achievement helps bridge astronomy's elusive 'MeV gap' by providing the clearest view yet of low-energy gamma rays.

t: Tracking Down a Mystery Beep By Giving a Coding Agent a Few Ears
r: This ingenious project shows how pairing software agents with physical sensors can solve real-world problems. Using web-audio listeners to triangulate an elusive household noise is a wonderfully nerdy engineering win.
s: Simon Willison recently used a Python web server and web-based audio listeners scattered around a room to help a coding agent triangulate an intermittent, mysterious beep. By leveraging the Web Audio API on spare devices, the system successfully located a buried carbon monoxide detector emitting a low-battery chirp.

t: The Simons Observatory is Online and Surveying the Cosmic Microwave Background
r: The Simons Observatory brings unprecedented precision to our study of the early universe. Searching for tiny fluctuations tied to primordial gravitational waves gets us closer than ever to observational evidence of the Big Bang.
s: The Simons Observatory has officially come online to survey the Cosmic Microwave Background with greater detail than ever before. The project aims to detect tiny fluctuations caused by primordial gravitational waves, offering potential slam-dunk evidence for the Big Bang.

t: Watch Jupiter's Moons Eclipse and Occult One Another
r: Jupiter's four bright Galilean moons frequently cross paths, but watching them actively eclipse and occult one another offers a fantastic observational challenge for backyard astronomers over the coming months.
s: Jupiter routinely occults and eclipses its four bright Galilean moons, and over the next few months, the moons will begin eclipsing and occulting one another in a rare alignment.

t: Microscopic Space Dust Reveals A Hidden Reservoir Of "Heavy Water" Beyond Neptune
r: Tiny samples can carry massive clues about planetary origins, and finding an ancient heavy water reservoir beyond Neptune rewrites our understanding of how volatile elements distributed during solar system formation.
s: Dust grains collected by high-altitude aircraft have helped researchers solve a mystery about the early Solar System, indicating that the region beyond Neptune once harbored an isolated reservoir of heavy water.

t: Linux in a Browser Tab
r: Running a complete kernel via WebAssembly at a decent fraction of native speed is a brilliant engineering feat that makes tinkering with shells and packages infinitely more accessible on the go.
s: Unkernel packages Linux 7.x as a single WebAssembly module complete with an MMU, allowing users to run a full Linux environment with a shell, package manager, and persistent storage directly inside a browser tab.

t: Introducing Staged Publishing on NuGet.org
r: Staged publishing gives maintainers crucial control over release boundaries, allowing teams to prep security fixes and major updates without exposing unfinished packages prematurely.
s: NuGet.org has introduced staged publishing, allowing all package publishers to upload, prepare, and validate packages privately before making an explicit decision to push them live.

t: NASA Data Clinches First-of-Its-Kind Stellar Merger
r: Catching a stellar merger in the act and tracing its history using Webb data provides remarkable insights into the dynamic life cycles of binary star systems.
s: Observations from the James Webb Space Telescope have provided the definitive evidence needed to reconstruct the events before, during, and after a unique binary star merger in the Andromeda galaxy.

t: Not-So-Large Language Model Fits On a Floppy Disk
r: Building a functional transformer model that runs on MS-DOS from a single floppy disk is a delightful exercise in retro-computing constraints and extreme minimalism.
s: A compact transformer model written in Turbo C 2.0 targets 486DX or Pentium processors and runs on DOS, packing 3,500 facts into a 380 KB network that fits entirely on a single floppy disk.

t: Veliki Kalnik Castle in Koprivnica, Croatia
r: Castles built directly into natural rock formations carry incredible histories, especially when local folklore involves royal gratitude paid in plums during a Mongol invasion.
s: Perched on a jagged ridge in northern Croatia since the 13th century, Veliki Kalnik Castle is tied to a local legend where starving defenders under siege were kept alive by villagers supplying plums.

t: Milky Way versus Aurora in a Dazzling Night Sky Display
r: This Astronomy Picture of the Day captures a striking visual juxtaposition between the ancient galactic band of the Milky Way and a vibrant auroral ribbon. It highlights the beauty of night-sky phenomena without requiring complex gear or falling into hype. It's a clean, gorgeous reminder of what lies just beyond our atmosphere.
s: An Astronomy Picture of the Day feature highlights a stunning night sky view where the central arch of our Milky Way appears alongside a glowing auroral ribbon. The image demonstrates the dramatic interplay between distant galactic structures and localized atmospheric light shows.

t: Rare Binary Star Emits Radio Pulses Every Few Minutes
r: Long Period Radio Transients are fascinating objects, and this discovery helps astronomers narrow down the progenitors for Type Ia supernovae. It provides a solid astrophysical puzzle about a white dwarf paired with a main-sequence star rather than the usual red dwarf. It hits all the right notes for deep space discovery and empirical observation.
s: Astronomers have found a Long Period Radio Transient roughly 5,000 light-years away consisting of a white dwarf and a main-sequence star. While the exact source of the periodic radio pulses remains uncertain, the discovery helps researchers understand potential progenitors for Type Ia supernova explosions.

t: Weaving a 3D Printed Pixel Clock Without Tedious Jumper Wires
r: Hardware hackers love addressable LEDs, but the wiring and soldering can become tedious very quickly. This creative pixel clock project solves that mechanical bottleneck by weaving a continuous strip directly through a 3D-printed enclosure. It is a clever engineering shortcut that makes builds more accessible.
s: A newly designed 3D printed pixel clock lets makers build a 7-by-19 display by carefully weaving a continuous 2.5-meter addressable LED strip through the frame. This clever mechanical approach eliminates the need for tedious manual jumper wiring or individual soldering.

t: Water in the Ancient Iranian Desert Through Ingenious Qanat Tunnels
r: Ancient engineering achievements like the Persian qanat system offer incredible insights into how civilizations solved massive logistical problems long before modern tools. Examining how mathematicians like Al-Karaji documented these subterranean aqueducts is a wonderful look at historical resource management.
s: Constructed across the arid Iranian Plateau, an extensive network of underground tunnels known as qanats allowed ancient civilizations to thrive by tapping mountain water sources. Guided by historical treatises like those of mathematician Al-Karaji, workers dug thousands of vertical shafts and gentle subterranean channels to bring water safely to the surface.

t: Annalee Newitz Discusses Slime Mold Characters and Novel Writing
r: Annalee Newitz always brings a thoughtful, grounded perspective to science fiction storytelling. Hearing an author talk about becoming obsessed with slime mold characters offers a fun glimpse into the mechanics of world-building and speculative craft.
s: In an interview discussing their novel A Wall Is Also A Road, author Annalee Newitz dives into the creative process behind writing unusual science fiction characters. The conversation explores how a background in journalism and nonfiction helps inform inventive speculative futures.

t: Rare Atmospheric River and Waterspouts Strike the San Francisco Bay Area
r: Severe weather events like atmospheric rivers and rare California waterspouts make for compelling meteorological study without straying into routine daily forecasts. It documents unusual atmospheric instability and radar-tracked storm cells hitting the coast.
s: A potent atmospheric river system brought rare severe weather to Northern California, triggering tornado warnings in Santa Cruz County and spawning twin waterspouts over San Francisco Bay. The unusual storm highlighted intense localized atmospheric instability along the West Coast.

t: Voyager 1 Reaches a Milestone of One Light-Day From Earth

s: Project Scientist Linda Spilker discusses the latest updates from the Voyager probes, highlighting the milestone moment as Voyager 1 reaches a distance of one light-day from Earth.

t: Newer Rigol Scopes Get a Custom Linux Firmware Layer
r: Open-operating-system firmware projects for modern test equipment give hardware hackers vastly more control without destroying factory safety nets. Running dual operating systems off an SD card is a brilliant hack for electronics labs.
s: A developer has created a custom Open Operating System firmware for DHO series Rigol oscilloscopes that runs alongside the factory OS via the built-in SD card, offering deeper user control.

t: Webb Reveals Galaxy Outflows Regulate Star Formation at Cosmic Noon
r: NASA's James Webb Space Telescope continues to unravel the mysteries of galaxy evolution by examining massive gaseous outflows. Understanding these mechanisms helps explain how galaxies regulate star formation during peak cosmic epochs.
s: NASA's Webb telescope reveals that massive gaseous outflows play a crucial role in regulating star formation and ultimate habitability in galaxies during the era of cosmic noon.

t: Building a Custom Cassette Mechanism From Scratch
r: When off-the-shelf parts disappear, passionate makers design their own mechanical chassis and custom controllers. Using PCB substrates, brushless motors, and an optical mouse sensor for tape speed is an extraordinary mechanical engineering feat.
s: Maker Svofski is designing a custom cassette mechanism entirely from scratch using PCB chassis, dual brushless motors, and an optical mouse sensor to monitor tape speed for data storage.

t: A Visual History of 49 Drill Holes by Curiosity on Mars
d: from the martian core samples dept.
r: Seeing the cumulative progress of robotic planetary exploration in a single image is always inspiring. This collage of drill holes highlights years of careful chemical analysis on the Martian surface.
s: A new collage from NASA showcases 49 distinct drill holes created by the Curiosity Mars rover as it gathers pulverized rock samples for onboard compositional analysis.

t: Rare Twin Waterspouts Form Over San Francisco Bay
r: Atmospheric river storms delivering rare and dramatic severe weather along the West Coast make for fascinating meteorological observation. Capturing simultaneous waterspouts over San Francisco Bay highlights the chaotic beauty of these events.
s: Recent severe storms sweeping through Northern California spawned rare twin waterspouts over the San Francisco Bay, caught clearly on video during an active atmospheric river.

t: A Supernova 50 Million Light-Years Away Gives Astronomers a Close-Up Show
r: A nearby Type Ia supernova provides astronomers with an ideal laboratory for detailed follow-up observations as its light fades over time. Because these stellar explosions serve as standard candles in cosmology, catching one relatively close by helps refine our understanding of cosmic distances.
s: A newly detected Type Ia supernova in a spiral galaxy about 50 million light-years away is close enough for astronomers and astrophotographers to track its fading light. The explosion of this white dwarf offers valuable data for refining distance measurements across the cosmos.

t: Perseverance Rover Captures Ghostly, Silica-Rich Rocks at 'Idubi' on Mars
d: from the pale red dot dept.
r: Mars rover updates continue to provide tangible evidence of ancient aqueous environments through high-resolution imagery and local geological sampling. Studying features like the silica-rich rocks in the Idubi area helps reconstruct the planet's watery past.
s: NASA's Perseverance rover used its Mastcam-Z camera to photograph bright, silica-rich rocks within the ancient Martian crust outside Jezero crater. These formations serve as lingering reminders of ancient aqueous systems that once shaped the landscape.

t: NOAA Forecasts Kp 4.67 as G1 Geomagnetic Storm Watch Remains Active
o: The Watchers - Watching the world evolve and transform
r: Space weather tracking provides essential situational awareness for high-latitude operations and potential aurora displays without resorting to exaggerated claims. Keeping tabs on NOAA forecasts helps observers anticipate shifts in the magnetosphere.
s: NOAA maintained a G1 geomagnetic storm watch while forecasting Kp index levels reaching 4.67. The conditions offer favorable opportunities for high-latitude skywatchers to spot aurora activity.

t: A Zero-Gravity Binocular Chair Makes Long Nights of Stargazing Comfortable
r: Practical equipment hacks that solve real observational fatigue are always welcome in amateur astronomy and DIY hardware circles. This motorized zero-gravity chair build provides a clever way to keep binoculars trained on the zenith without straining your arms.
s: Maker Dave Selinger designed a portable zero-gravity lounge chair outfitted with a bearing-mounted base and binocular-holding apparatus. The setup allows observers to scan the night sky comfortably from various angles while locking altitude and azimuth.

t: ESP32-Powered Wi-Fi Interference Detector Categories Stray Signals
r: Hardware projects utilizing software-defined radio techniques to analyze local RF environments offer a fun intersection of microcontrollers and wireless engineering. Categorizing noise types makes troubleshooting interference both educational and practical.
s: An open-source project built around an ESP32-C5 microcontroller uses software-defined radio to scan 2.4GHz and 5GHz Wi-Fi bands for interference. The portable device can classify detected noise into four distinct patterns, helping users distinguish between leaky appliances and external signals.

t: Satellite Images Show the Rapid Disappearance of Tropical Glacial Ice on Puncak Jaya
r: Satellite imagery comparisons provide striking, undeniable evidence of long-term environmental changes across rare glacial formations. Observing these shifts from orbit highlights the vulnerability of high-altitude ice fields.
s: Side-by-side false-color satellite images captured by Landsat missions in 1988 and 2026 reveal the dramatic retreat of glacial ice on Indonesia's Puncak Jaya. Only a few small fragments of blue ice remain where extensive ridgetops were once capped frozen.

t: Netflix Sets Early 2027 Premiere for Season 2 of '3 Body Problem'
r: Clear scheduling news for ambitious science fiction adaptations gives fans a reliable horizon for upcoming storytelling. It is helpful to track production timelines without getting bogged down in industry gossip.
s: Netflix confirmed that the second season of its television adaptation of Liu Cixin's novels will arrive early next year. The upcoming episodes continue the complex narrative established in the first season.

t: Webb Captures Stellar Jets and Star Formation in NGC 7129
r: The James Webb Space Telescope continues to deliver breathtaking infrared imagery of star-forming regions. This detailed look at NGC 7129 illustrates how gravity and energetic stellar jets interact during the birth of new stars.
s: Using its infrared instruments, NASA's James Webb Space Telescope has captured a detailed image of the star-forming region NGC 7129, highlighting the complex processes of gas compression and stellar jets.

t: New Superconducting Magnets Upgrade the Large Hadron Collider
r: Upgrading particle accelerators requires overcoming immense materials-science hurdles, such as handling brittle niobium-tin conductors. It is a fascinating look at the engineering required to push the Large Hadron Collider past 12 Tesla.
s: As part of its ongoing high-luminosity upgrade phase, the Large Hadron Collider is incorporating advanced niobium-tin superconducting magnets that significantly increase magnetic field strength compared to previous designs.

t: Building a Network-Attached Storage Device for Sony Mavica Floppy Disks
r: Combining vintage Sony Mavica digital cameras that used 3.5-inch floppies with modern dual-processor architectures is peak hacker ingenuity. This project cleverly bridges eras with Greaseweazle and ESP32 hardware.
s: A clever hardware hacker has built a dedicated network-attached storage device for vintage Sony Mavica digital cameras, using an RP2354 to read floppy disks and an ESP32-S3 to serve the files over a web interface.

t: Monitoring AC Power Grid Frequency with an Arduino Uno
r: Tracking power grid frequency drift provides a tangible, low-level look at real-world electrical infrastructure. Using an optocoupler and an Arduino to log years of grid data in just bytes is wonderfully resourceful.

t: Rare Fogbow Photographed in Kayl

t: Building High-Power Loop Antennas with 3D-Printed Gear Reductions
r: Radio enthusiasts often face severe space constraints for outdoor antennas, making compact loop antennas a clever alternative. This build tackles the tricky engineering problem of managing high transmit power and precise tuning without expensive vintage gear reductions.

t: NGC 206 and the Star Clouds of Andromeda
d: from the deep space imaging dept.

s: PancakeSlicer is a new open project designed to generate non-planar toolpaths for standard 3-axis 3D printers. By modifying hardware clearances and rethinking top-layer slicing algorithms, it enables smoother upper surfaces that eliminate the familiar staircase artifact.

t: First Foreign Astronaut to Visit China's Tiangong Space Station

t: Writing Your Own PostScript Interpreter from Scratch

t: Minnesota Park Named International Dark Sky Place of the Year
r: Recognizing pristine dark-sky locations helps protect night-sky visibility and local nocturnal ecosystems from encroaching light pollution. Regional successes in dark-sky conservation offer a model for preserving stargazing heritage.

t: Solving the Space Junk Crisis with Economics and Control
